dev-0000 (single): On unified-memory machines, how does the book say large mixture-of-experts models compare in fitting and decoding speed to dense models with about the same total size?
reference: Large mixture-of-experts models fit and decode faster than dense models of similar total size.
first relevant chunk at rank 1; context: [1] chapter_appendix-tools-for-deep-learning/hardware#005 (relevant), [2] chapter_transformers/moe#019, [3] chapter_transformers/further-reading#021, [4] chapter_transformers/moe#022, [5] chapter_transformers/moe#021
answer: On unified-memory machines, large models fit but decode slowly due to the lower bandwidth of system RAM compared to VRAM [1]. However, a mixture-of-experts (MoE) model runs only a few of its expert networks for each token, so it reads only its active parameters [1]. Consequently, an MoE model decodes faster than a dense model of similar total size because it accesses fewer parameters per token [1]. This allows large models to fit within the memory capacity while maintaining a faster decoding speed than their dense counterparts [1].
